name: sf-health-analyzer
description: Salesforce Architecture Health & Insights — Built with security-first AI. No sensitive data ever leaves your org. Enterprise-grade analysis of Apex quality, automation complexity, data model health, test coverage, security, and performance.

sfHealthAnalyzer.rules.maxTriggersPerObj.description: Maximum number of triggers allowed per object

sfHealthAnalyzer.rules.maxFlowsPerObject.description: Maximum number of flows allowed per object

sfHealthAnalyzer.rules.maxTriggerLines.description: Maximum lines of code allowed in a trigger

sfHealthAnalyzer.rules.maxClassLines.description: Maximum lines of code allowed in a class

sfHealthAnalyzer.rules.maxMethodLines.description: Maximum lines of code allowed in a method

sfHealthAnalyzer.rules.maxValidationRule.description: Maximum validation rules allowed per object

sfHealthAnalyzer.rules.maxProcessBuilder.description: Maximum Process Builders allowed per object (should be 0 - use Flows)

sfHealthAnalyzer.scoring.weights.description: Weights for each health score category (must sum to 100)

sfHealthAnalyzer.analysis.includeOrgMeta.description: Include metadata from connected Salesforce org in analysis

sfHealthAnalyzer.analysis.largeDataVolum.description: Record count threshold to flag large data volume risks

sfHealthAnalyzer.codeAnalyzer.enabled.description: Delegate static Apex/LWC code analysis to Salesforce Code Analyzer (sf code-analyzer run) instead of the built-in rules. Requires the 'code-analyzer' CLI plugin and a Java runtime; falls back to built-in rules when they are unavailable.

sfHealthAnalyzer.codeAnalyzer.ruleSelect.description: Rule selector passed to 'sf code-analyzer run --rule-selector' (e.g. Recommended, all, Security, pmd).

sfHealthAnalyzer.codeAnalyzer.runGraphEn.description: Also run the Salesforce Graph Engine (sfge) data-flow security rules. More thorough but significantly slower and memory-heavy on large codebases.

sfHealthAnalyzer.ai.enabled.description: Enable AI-powered issue explanations via GitHub Copilot

enumDescriptions: Safe: 100% local analysis, no AI, no external data sharing
Standard: AI summarises aggregated insights only, no sensitive data shared
Advanced: Enriched AI insights, still no raw code or PII
sfHealthAnalyzer.ai.securityMode.description: Default security mode for org scanning. Controls AI usage and data handling. Users can override per-session via the scan mode selection dialog.

enumDescriptions: Auto: use a VS Code Language Model provider if available, otherwise the configured local/custom endpoint
VS Code Language Model API only (any installed provider — Copilot's Claude/GPT/Gemini, Codex, third-party)
Local / custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint only (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, OpenAI, Codex, Azure)
sfHealthAnalyzer.ai.provider.description: Which AI backend to use. Models are discovered dynamically — not restricted to GitHub Copilot.

sfHealthAnalyzer.ai.preferredModel.description: Preferred AI model selector. 'auto' picks the best available model; otherwise a discovered model id ('<vendor>/<family>' for a VS Code LM model, or 'custom:<model>' for a local/custom endpoint). Normally set from the model picker in the dashboard rather than edited by hand.

sfHealthAnalyzer.ai.custom.baseUrl.description: Base URL of an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint for the local/custom AI backend. Defaults to Ollama. Examples: Ollama 'http://localhost:11434/v1', LM Studio 'http://localhost:1234/v1', OpenAI 'https://api.openai.com/v1'.

sfHealthAnalyzer.ai.custom.model.description: Model name for the local/custom AI backend (e.g. 'qwen2.5-coder', 'llama3.1', 'gpt-4o-mini'). Required to enable the local/custom backend. Tool-capable models also power Ask the Architect's live org queries.

sfHealthAnalyzer.ai.custom.apiKey.description: Optional API key (sent as a Bearer token) for the local/custom AI endpoint. Leave empty for local servers like Ollama; set it for OpenAI / Azure / hosted endpoints.

sfHealthAnalyzer.queryExplain.enabled.description: Enable live query selectivity analysis via the Salesforce Tooling API EXPLAIN endpoint (requires connected org)

sfHealthAnalyzer.ctaArchitecture.enabled.description: Enable CTA-tier architectural checks: callout-in-trigger, heap-risk SOQL, LDV density, licence alignment

sfHealthAnalyzer.plugins.description: Paths to third-party plugin files that contribute additional analysis rules. Paths can be absolute or relative to the workspace root.

sfHealthAnalyzer.scaleCenter.enabled.description: Enable Scale Center / EventLogFile performance analytics (requires Enterprise Edition or above)

sfHealthAnalyzer.lwc.enabled.description: Enable LWC component quality analysis from workspace files

sfHealthAnalyzer.debt.sprintHoursPerCycl.description: Estimated hours of debt-remediation capacity per sprint cycle (default 16 = 20% of a 2-week sprint)

sfHealthAnalyzer.userGovernance.enabled.description: Enable User Governance analysis (dormant users, super-admins, role hierarchy depth)

sfHealthAnalyzer.profileSecurity.enabled.description: Enable Profile & Permission Set security analysis (dangerous permissions audit)

sfHealthAnalyzer.staleMetadata.enabled.description: Enable Stale Metadata detection (reports and dashboards not modified in 180+ days)

sfHealthAnalyzer.orgInventory.enabled.description: Enable Org Inventory analysis (installed packages, Visualforce pages, custom labels)

scripts.compile: npm run build:webview && npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.js
scripts.package: npm run build:webview && npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.js --production
scripts.build:webview: cd webview-ui && npm install && npm run build
scripts.pretest: npm run compile-tests && npm run compile && npm run lint
